title: Kummer computations on the line and the punctured line
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $k$, let $N\geq1$, and put $m=\ell^N$ and $R=\mathbf Z/m\mathbf Z$. Let $A$ be a finite free $R$-module of rank $r\geq0$. Consider the smooth separated affine connected curves $\mathbf A^1_k=\operatorname{Spec}k[t]$ and $\mathbf G_{m,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$ [def-sc-curves], with cohomology on their small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Write $\mu_m(U)=\{u\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times:u^m=1\}$, an etale sheaf of $R$-modules, and let $A_C$ be the constant sheaf with value $A$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Put $A(1)=\mu_m\otimes_{R_C}A_C$, using the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Choose a primitive $m$-th root of unity $\zeta\in k$.

For every integer $q\geq0$:

1. $H^0(\mathbf A^1_k,A(1))\cong A$ and $H^q(\mathbf A^1_k,A(1))=0$ for $q>0$.
2. $H^0(\mathbf G_{m,k},A(1))\cong A$, and $H^q(\mathbf G_{m,k},A(1))=0$ for $q>1$. In both degree-zero isomorphisms the map from $A$ sends $a$ to the constant section $\zeta\otimes a$; restriction from the affine line to the punctured line corresponds to the identity of $A$.
3. Let $\delta:\Gamma(\mathbf G_{m,k},\mathbf G_m)\to H^1(\mathbf G_{m,k},\mu_m)$ be the connecting map for the Kummer sequence [def-sc-kummer-sequence], and put $\kappa_m(t)=\delta(t)$. The $R$-linear map
$$
A\longrightarrow H^1(\mathbf G_{m,k},A(1)),\qquad
 a\longmapsto H^1(i_a)(\kappa_m(t)),\qquad
 i_a:\mu_m\longrightarrow A(1),\quad x\longmapsto x\otimes a,
$$
is an isomorphism. For $A=R$, it sends $1$ to the Kummer generator $\kappa_m(t)$; for general $A$ the group is free of rank $r$ over $R$.

All these cohomology groups are finite $R$-modules. The identifications are natural for $R$-linear maps $A\to B$ of finite free $R$-modules. More explicitly, the coefficient comparison
$$
H^q(C,\mu_m)\otimes_R A\longrightarrow H^q(C,A(1)),\qquad
 x\otimes a\longmapsto H^q(i_a)(x),
$$
is an isomorphism for either curve $C$ and every $q\geq0$. Thus coefficient base change is compatible with the displayed degree-zero sections and Kummer maps: for a finite free commutative $R$-algebra $S$, scalar extension gives $H^q(C,A(1))\otimes_R S\cong H^q(C,\mu_m\otimes_R(A\otimes_R S))$, sending $\kappa_m(t)\otimes a\otimes s$ to the class with coefficient $a\otimes s$.

proof.text: Apply the root-coefficient computation with m=ell^N and the given primitive root. Invertibility follows by taking a power and mapping scalars. This supplies the actual degree-zero sections, their restriction identity, root vanishings, and the actual degree-one Kummer generator.

proof.text: Apply finite-free coefficient comparison in every degree. Tensoring the degree-zero root equivalence and the punctured degree-one root equivalence with A gives the displayed generator formulas. A tensor factor that is zero gives zero; all remaining root groups are equivalent to the finite residue ring, so all tensor cohomology groups are finite. Naturality is the coefficient-map formula. Tensor associativity and the comparison for A tensor S give scalar extension and its pure-tensor formula.

proof.text: Conjugate root restriction tensor the identity on A by the two coefficient comparisons to define restriction. The tensor formula proves both required equations. For uniqueness conjugate any proposed map by the same comparisons; extensionality on pure tensors forces equality. The argument includes A=0.
